title: When the Trail Falls
premise: Elodie Delacroix, estranged from his famous archaeologist father Armand, is summoned when the elder's upriver expedition goes silent. Following the river into unmapped country, Elodie finds the camp ransacked, the team scattered, and evidence that his father uncovered a pre-colonial vault whose artifacts grant real political power to whoever holds them. As he gathers the survivors and races the flood season downriver, Elodie must decide whether to protect his father's secret—as loyalty demands—or expose it, since the truth alone can save them from the expedition's financier, who will kill to keep the find buried and claimable. In the end Elodie chooses truth: he surrenders the vault's location to the national museum, lets his father face ruin, and brings every living member of the team home.
about_author: Zephyrine Ashgrove spent a decade leading river expeditions through remote interior basins before turning to fiction full-time. Her novels are known for their unsentimental wilderness detail and their obsession with what families bury.

chapters.title: The Letter That Smelled of River Water
chapters.summary: Elodie, working a salvage dig in the lowlands, receives a telegram: his father's expedition has missed two scheduled check-ins. POV Elodie. The beat is reluctant duty—the pull of a name he swore to stop answering.

chapters.title: What the Museum Wouldn't Say
chapters.summary: In the capital, Elodie confronts the sponsoring institute and meets Odile Ferrand, the expedition's coldly helpful financier. She gives him a radio frequency and a warning. POV Elodie. Beat: unease beneath official politeness.

chapters.title: Packing for a Place That Doesn't Want You
chapters.summary: Elodie assembles gear and hires boatman Tomas Reyes, who once worked with Armand and owes him a debt he resents. POV Elodie. Beat: grudging partnership forged over cargo manifests and old grievances.

chapters.title: Upriver, Where Maps Go Thin
chapters.summary: The journey begins; rapids, heat, and Tomas's pointed silence about the last time he saw Armand. POV Elodie. Beat: the wilderness asserting itself as a character that keeps score.

chapters.title: Static on Frequency Nine
chapters.summary: At night Elodie raises the expedition frequency and catches a fragment—a woman's voice counting down numbers—then nothing. POV Elodie. Beat: hope sharpened into dread.

chapters.title: The Village That Turned Its Backs
chapters.summary: A riverside settlement refuses to discuss the foreigners who passed upstream; an elder leaves a carved token in Elodie's boat unasked. POV Elodie. Beat: the sense of being warned by people who've already been hurt.

chapters.title: First Blood on the Water
chapters.summary: A second boat shadows them; shots crack across the water at dusk and Tomas runs the rapids blind to lose them. POV Elodie. Beat: fear made physical—the trip is no longer a rescue but a pursuit.

chapters.title: Camp One, Empty and Wrong
chapters.summary: They reach the first basecamp: tents slashed from inside, instruments smashed, and a ledger page showing Armand recorded a discovery weeks before the official log admits. POV Elodie. Beat: betrayal surfacing in his father's own handwriting.

chapters.title: The Survivor Who Won't Stop Walking
chapters.summary: They find botanist Ines Okafor wandering, feverish, muttering about 'the door under the falls.' They treat her; she begs them to go home. POV alternating Elodie/Ines. Beat: pity tangled with frustration.

chapters.title: What Ines Saw at the Falls
chapters.summary: Ines recounts the vault's discovery and how Armand ordered it sealed and hidden—not from scholars, she says, but from Ferrand. POV Ines. Beat: the theme crystallizes—loyalty to a man versus loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: Ferrand's Second Boat
chapters.summary: The pursuing vessel is Ferrand's private security, led by a quiet man named Brac. A captured radio reveals orders: recover the artifacts, leave no witnesses. POV Elodie. Beat: the stakes turn mortal and personal.

chapters.title: The Portage Nobody Survives Twice
chapters.summary: A brutal overland portage around gorge rapids; Tomas injures his shoulder, and Elodie must lead for the first time. POV Elodie. Beat: competence earned under pressure—the son becomes more than the father's child.

chapters.title: Camp Two and the Man in the Tree
chapters.summary: At the second camp they find surveyor Lukas Brand alive, hiding, convinced everyone left is compromised. His paranoia nearly gets someone killed. POV Brand. Beat: isolation corroding trust.

chapters.title: Armand's Journal, First Reading
chapters.summary: Brand surrenders pages of Armand's journal: the vault predates every known culture here, and its contents could rewrite ownership of the entire valley. POV Elodie. Beat: awe curdling into greed's shadow—he feels the pull himself.

chapters.title: The Token Speaks
chapters.summary: The carved token matches markings at the falls; a hunter from the village appears, offering passage if Elodie swears the things stay buried. POV Elodie. Beat: an alliance offered on terms that cost him something.

chapters.title: Brac Closes the River
chapters.summary: Brac's men burn the downstream village's boats to trap them; the hunter's family is threatened. POV Brac, briefly humanized. Beat: the antagonist revealed as a man doing arithmetic with lives.

chapters.title: Descent Into the Green Dark
chapters.summary: The party cuts inland toward the falls through rainforest, losing supplies, gaining a terrible intimacy. POV Ines. Beat: endurance as devotion—each character shows what they'd sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Door Under the Falls
chapters.summary: They reach the vault: a stone mouth behind falling water, sealed exactly as Armand left it—and freshly chiseled open from the other side. POV Elodie. Beat: dread of arrival; the secret is already loose.

chapters.title: Inside, the Weight of Gold
chapters.summary: Within: artifacts of impossible preservation, including documents proving the valley was never ceded. Elodie photographs everything. POV Elodie. Beat: temptation at its peak—one crate would buy every future he's ever wanted.

chapters.title: My Father, Alive and Unrepentant
chapters.summary: They find Armand at a hidden cache, wounded, guarding crates. Father and son meet with twenty years of silence between them. POV alternating. Beat: reunion as confrontation—love expressed only as accusation.

chapters.title: Why He Sealed It
chapters.summary: Armand explains: he hid the find because Ferrand's contract gave her claim rights, and the documents prove the valley belongs to its peoples, not to any backer. POV Armand. Beat: sympathy without absolution.

chapters.title: The Ambush at the Cache
chapters.summary: Brac attacks at dawn. In the firefight the cache burns; Tomas takes a bullet shielding Elodie. POV Elodie. Beat: grief as tuition—the cost of the secret becomes blood.

chapters.title: Tomas's Debt, Paid
chapters.summary: Tomas survives but can't travel fast; he confesses his old debt to Armand and releases it, choosing to stay behind as decoy. POV Tomas. Beat: loyalty freely given, finally understood.

chapters.title: Running the Flood Season
chapters.summary: Rains break early; the river rises. The party must run water no one runs this time of year. POV Elodie. Beat: nature indifferent to human quarrels, terrifying and fair.

chapters.title: The Radio Answers
chapters.summary: Elodie broadcasts the vault's coordinates and contents openly—to the museum, the press, the village elders—burning Ferrand's secrecy advantage. POV Elodie. Beat: the thematic hinge; truth chosen over protection.

chapters.title: Armand's Fury
chapters.summary: Armand rages that exposure destroys his life's work and endangers the valley; Elodie answers that burial served only his pride. POV Armand. Beat: the estrangement named at last—two kinds of love, both wrong.

chapters.title: Brac's Last Order
chapters.summary: With the secret public, Brac's mission changes to silencing witnesses. He corners them at a mission outpost. POV Brac. Beat: the corrupted man confronting orders even he hesitates to follow.

chapters.title: The Mission Outpost Standoff
chapters.summary: A tense siege; Brand redeems his paranoia with a clever counter-signal that brings river police. Brac withdraws, promising the delta. POV Brand. Beat: trust rebuilt through action, not words.

chapters.title: Downriver Through the Drowned Forest
chapters.summary: The flooded forest passage: silent paddling, drowned cattle, the hunter guiding where charts fail. POV Ines. Beat: eerie calm before the final storm; gratitude taking root.

chapters.title: Ferrand at the Delta
chapters.summary: Ferrand waits at the river mouth with lawyers, money, and a final offer: Armand's reputation laundered, Elodie funded for life, in exchange for the originals. POV Elodie. Beat: corruption's most reasonable voice.

chapters.title: The Offer He Refuses
chapters.summary: Elodie declines; Ferrand pivots to threats against the villagers. The hunter steps forward and speaks the valley's claim aloud, on record. POV Elodie. Beat: courage contagious—the powerless become parties.

chapters.title: Brac's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Brac, learning Ferrand planned to discard him, turns state's evidence rather than die for her arithmetic. POV Brac. Beat: power devouring its own instrument.

chapters.title: The Hearing on the Dock
chapters.summary: An impromptu inquiry: journals, photographs, the documents themselves entered as evidence while the river rises around them. POV Elodie. Beat: truth as procedure—unglamorous, decisive.

chapters.title: Armand Breaks
chapters.summary: Confronted with his falsified logs, Armand collapses—not denying guilt but begging Elodie to understand why. POV Armand. Beat: the father finally seen whole: brilliant, cowardly, loving.

chapters.title: What the Valley Keeps
chapters.summary: The court awards stewardship to the valley's peoples; the vault is sealed under their law, not forgotten. The hunter returns the token. POV Elodie. Beat: justice that costs the hero his inheritance.

chapters.title: Father and Son, Unfinished
chapters.summary: Armand, disgraced, asks nothing; Elodie offers him a place on the next honest dig. It isn't forgiveness yet—it's a door. POV Elodie. Beat: reconciliation begun, not completed.

chapters.title: The Long Paddle Home
chapters.summary: The surviving team travels downriver together, mourning their dead, arguing, laughing once. POV Ines. Beat: the expedition brought home—the promise kept.

chapters.title: Epitaphs Written in Mud
chapters.summary: Burials at the riverbank for those lost; Tomas, recovered, carves names into hardwood. POV Elodie. Beat: grief given shape; the wilderness forgives nothing, but memory holds.

chapters.title: The Dig That Tells the Truth
chapters.summary: Months later, Elodie leads a transparent excavation under joint stewardship, publishing everything in real time. POV Elodie. Beat: vocation reborn from wreckage.

chapters.title: When the Trail Falls Silent
chapters.summary: Final image: Elodie at the falls, listening to water over the sealed door, at peace with what stays buried. A letter arrives from his father. He reads it twice, then pockets it unfinished. POV Elodie. Beat: quiet resolution—inheritance redefined as responsibility, not possession.
